title: Employee Medical Check-Up
intro:
An employee medical check-up is a medical examination conducted to assess the health condition of employees or prospective employees in the workplace. Its purpose is to maintain workers' health and prevent illnesses that may affect productivity.

In addition to benefiting employees, workplace medical check-ups also help reduce sick leave, improve productivity, and enhance the company's reputation.
types_intro: Employee medical check-ups are categorized based on the time of examination and the type of work.
timing_title: A. Employee Medical Check-Up Based on Timing
timing_intro: Depending on when the examination is conducted, employee medical check-ups are divided into three types:
pre_body: As the name suggests, this examination is conducted before a prospective employee begins work. It is intended to assess physical fitness and prevent the transmission of infectious diseases before employment. Common examinations include complete physical examination, laboratory tests, and chest X-ray.
periodic_body: A periodic medical check-up is a routine health examination conducted according to the occupational risks in the employee's work environment. This examination is generally performed at least once a year.
special_body: A special medical check-up is conducted to detect health risks or the effects of specific job conditions on certain groups of employees, including:
special_1: Employees who have experienced work-related accidents
jobtype_title: B. Employee Medical Check-Up Based on Job Type
jobtype_intro: Since every occupation has its own health risks, medical examinations should be tailored to each employee's work environment. Examples include:
jobtype_1: Employees working in noisy environments, such as factories or machine maintenance areas, require audiometry tests to assess hearing function.
jobtype_2: Employees exposed to respiratory hazards, such as cement factories or automotive paint spraying facilities, require spirometry tests to evaluate lung function.
prep_title: Preparing for an Employee Medical Check-Up
prep_intro: Before undergoing a medical check-up, employees are advised to prepare by fasting and maintaining good health. Preparation includes:
prep_1: Fasting for 8–12 hours before the examination, depending on the required tests.
prep_2: Wearing a short-sleeved shirt to make blood collection easier.
prep_3: Getting 7–9 hours of sleep the night before, as lack of sleep may affect blood pressure, heart rate, and body temperature results.
prep_note: If you have a history of certain medical conditions, please bring your previous medical examination results.
proc_intro: Employee medical check-ups generally include the following examinations:
lab_body: Samples of blood, urine, and, when required, stool are collected for laboratory analysis. Blood tests evaluate blood cell counts, organ function markers, blood sugar levels, cholesterol levels, liver function, and kidney function. Urinalysis is performed to detect urinary tract infections, diabetes, kidney disease, and liver disorders. Stool examination analyzes stool samples to detect digestive disorders, such as intestinal inflammation or gastroenteritis. This test is only included in specific medical check-up packages when required.
xray_body: An X-ray examination is performed to obtain images of internal organs, particularly the heart and lungs, to identify abnormalities or infections.
ecg_body: An electrocardiogram (ECG or EKG) records the heart's electrical activity by placing electrodes on the chest, arms, and legs. This examination helps detect heart rhythm abnormalities and other cardiac conditions.
audio_body: Audiometry is performed to evaluate hearing function by measuring the patient's ability to hear sounds at different frequencies and volumes.
spiro_body: Spirometry evaluates lung function using a device called a spirometer, which measures the amount of air inhaled and exhaled.
color_body: Color vision is commonly assessed using the Ishihara Test, in which patients identify numbers hidden within colored dot patterns.
physical_body: The doctor will perform a general physical examination, including blood pressure measurement, height and weight measurement, vision assessment, and overall physical examination.
result_intro: Medical check-up results are evaluated based on the employee's workplace and job responsibilities. The results are generally classified as:
result_1: Fit to Work – Healthy and medically fit for work.
result_2: Fit with Notes – Medically fit for work with certain recommendations or restrictions.
result_3: Unfit – Not medically fit for work.
closing: Employee medical check-ups play an important role in maintaining employee health, motivation, and productivity. At Amalia Medical Center, we offer comprehensive employee medical check-up packages to help companies ensure the overall health and well-being of their workforce.
